dedupe_keys.name: turning dataset for chatter diagnosis using machine learning

description: This Mendeley Data collection provides sensor signals from turning experiments for machine-learning diagnosis of chatter in a manufacturing process, supporting condition monitoring. Measurements come from two perpendicular single-axis accelerometers, a triaxial accelerometer, a microphone and a laser tachometer. The source distinguishes raw signals from all sensors and conditioned, labelled signals from one triaxial channel. Labels are no chatter, intermediate chatter, chatter and unknown. An Aluminium 6061 workpiece was turned on a Clausing-Gamet engine lathe with a coated insert and boring bar. Four tool stickout lengths were tested: 5.08, 6.35, 8.89 and 11.43 cm, each with several rotational-speed and cutting-depth settings. Coverage is these controlled cutting configurations; sample cadence, geographic location and acquisition dates are not stated in the inspected description. Two ZIP distribution descriptors identify raw and processed signal groups, but their internal data format is unknown. CC BY 4.0 terms are stated. The provider links experimental documentation alongside the distributions. No archive, README, experimental PDF or signal values were fetched.
